questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was the nice temperature and different climate in Australia that were drawing to me. And I thought it would be good to study in an English speaking country, so I could flette into social situations easier. That was definitely a good choice!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: GO ABROAD. pls. I cam here without any expectations and I have learned so much about different cultures, people, situations (and a bit of uni). I am definitely considering going again on my masters, it is just such a great opportunity to get some perspective on your own life at home.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I mean... It is of course a complicated matter, that being on top of you going away for so long. But you just gotta do it, and it will all be worth it in the end. Some information is a bit tricky to wrap your head around, but please just remind yourself that it is in everyones interest that you are going. So if something is really important, you will have the necessary guidens.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Hmm, I got a lot of emails from USYD (uni), but it was not too difficult to figure out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It is always difficult finding your way around in a new city. I just think that the housing situation around UNI is very badly organized and too expensive.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Flatmates.com
is the way to go. It is a jungle for sure, and you have to figure out yourself if you are the type of person who can manage not knowing were or when you are gonna find a housing for 2-4 weeks, or if you want to pay extra for the safety of student accomendation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I can just say that I got the jackpot. I met the greatest friends in the hostel I was staying at when I arrived, and 4 of us decided to find housing together. So now we live in a 10 person house in Glebe with other students, and that is great mate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sydney is an expensive city. But because there are so many exchange students, they take a loooot of money for Student accommodation. And it is not even that nice, so mostly you just pay for the safety. My advice is - live a little, you learn a lot from the frustrating proces of finding a home - but I do not know anyone who did not find a place in the end.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: USYD is really good at guiding you, but there are just a lot of formalia concerning study abroad.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a contact person from home who you can email. And most of it I just found out after I arrived. It is really easy to move your schedule around and change units, so do not stress too much about that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got all the help I needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my classes and I even swapped out three - you can do that within the first 14-21 days of study.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress it, they will make changes to your schedule anyways. If you can, keep your friday free. That is nice;)) And almost everyone does it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If I have to be honest, I did not really go on exchange to do a lot of studying. But I have been really surprised of how nice it has been to have a different way of learning and my units have been so amazing!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I mostly took 2. year classes ;))

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You have more tutorials which is really awesome (der kan KU seriøst godt lige lære noget). You get to discuss your readings and assignments in a safe space with only 15-25 students - I learned a lot from that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CRIM2602 Crime, Punishment and Society
SCLG2623 Sociology of Terror
EDUH4058 Sport and Learning in Australia
EDGU1003 Diet and Nutrition for Health and Sports

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved every one of my choices. Do yourself a favor and choose some easy subjects as well, so you have some more free time. Mine had a perfect balance, Crime, Punishment and Society was an amazing unit with a great teacher, I really loved doing the studying for that. But then Sport and Learning in Australia is really cool, because you basically just go out and watch Australian sports. It was a good way to get to know the culture, and have an easy unit;)) Diet and nutrition is also very chill and kind of interesting. Sociology of Terror was the perfect supplement for my other criminology unit.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I feel like the worst money is the ones you have to spend before you arrive. So danish insurance, insurance in Australia, TOEFL test, plane tickets and so on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I saw - save up a lot of money, because it is just more fun to be able to travel and enjoy yourself. I have gotten a job at a cafe, that helps and is culturally fun as well!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: USYD are not really good at social activities, you'll have to do that yourself. In the first week there are some things to sign up for, but apart from that just be open and invite yourself to things;)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have played a lot of tennis down here. I just bought som racquets on FB marketplace and then you can rent courts at uni.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Live in a hostel in the beginning;)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mate, there is too many things to do here. So just stay when your semester is over. I will be traveling for two months and that does not even get me that far. Just come down here and figure it out.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There are a lot of exchange students looking for friends, and everyone speaks the same language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to class. There are lots of Aussies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, they are absolutely great people. And Sydney is very multi cultural, so everyone is accepted and welcome!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That there is room for everyone, you can look exactly how you like and be who you want and everyone just finds it great, it is not even a spectacle. Just normal. I really love Sydney - mostly in the sun.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Just get through the application proces, it is what it is.
2. Safe up money, expect to spend 100k
3. Harris farmers market - cheap vegetables and just a great store.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hold tight and know that summer will come. But bring three pair of long pants though;))

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: living and getting to know a different city so well. It is amazing, Sydney has so many things to offer.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning with house hunting for sure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO GO GO. I am so extremely happy about the things I have learned and the friends I have gotten. This will be an experience for life!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
